summary:
Builder 1 (fixtures and Edge) is done. The full `lune run scripts/verify` is green: 650 pass, exit 0.

**Baseline.** I re-ran the plan's scripts on a copy of the committed tree (HEAD 7eb9914): tab, es29 rank, orders and contracts dif04. All four match the plan's [7] outputs exactly, so there was nothing to trace. Suite times before M3, quiet machine: --quick 18.90 s, full suite 163.57 s.

**What I built**
- **Fixtures:** Build.YM90 and a shared record type; Calibration (15 swords), Regression (34 records including the two union-blade bases), Cost (P1–P5, six speck variants, the X08 aliases, the 39 T-PERF-01 cases) and WorstDesigns (a copy of the docs file).
- **Adversarial:** A25, A26 (with its base as a variant) and A27; A14's relation is now bit-identical to F1.
- **Fixture checks:** three new specs plus a shared helper. They check every row bit for bit against the prototype, the canonical fixed point, margins (P4 exempt) and Physics' verdict and cleaned lists. WorstDesigns is checked bit for bit against the docs file.
- **Physics/Edge.luau:** the prototype's raster, outline and chains without % or //, with a total chain order, and the ladder charged (L6).
- **Edge.spec.luau:** T-EDG-01, 17 fast cases and 1 slow. P-DET and P-NOMUT for Edge.profile are included (L16).
- **Tol:** TOL_EDGE_REL 0.02 (L5).
- **docs/build/M3-notes.md:** the baseline section and my builder section.

**L1:** cutIndex re-measured on the committed tree matches the lead's 6-decimal column on every F and C row.

**L3 fell back to option (b).** I built the integer-lattice Douglas–Peucker first. It moved C15's Sharpening from 0.4291 to 0.4299, more than the 0.0005 the criterion allows, because of one exact tie. Edge now runs the prototype's float Douglas–Peucker, and all 64 fixture edges match the emulator bit for bit. With (b), the critic's Gen #131 still moves G by 0.0037 under a Y shift; that figure goes to O11.

**New finding for the lead.** The raster itself is not exactly translation-invariant at exact ties, in the prototype as well. On 4 of the 20 F and C fixtures a shift changes the result: C10 and C11 move Sharpening G by 0.0063 and 0.0031, over TOL_G_INVARIANT, and C09's cutIndex goes from 1 to 0.8842. Edge.spec lists these 4 as known moves and asserts every other shifted copy exact.

deviations: L3 fell back to option (b), as the lead's decision prescribes: the lattice rule's C15 Sharpening moved 0.0008, more than 0.0005. Edge therefore keeps the prototype's float Douglas–Peucker in blueprint XY. Item 6 on Gen designs asserts the raster within 1e-12 and EdgeLength within TOL_EDGE_REL, not bit-identity.

T-EDG-01 item 6 on F1–F5 and C01–C15 is not exact on every shifted copy, contrary to L3 (b)'s premise (measured on 5 fixtures only). Edge.spec pins 4 known moves (C05 +0.125 and C09 Z −0.037: raster; C10 and C11 +0.3317: outline). Those 4 are checked only for EdgeLength within TOL_EDGE_REL plus the part that holds; every other copy is asserted exact.
'Printed, not asserted' values are not printed: no spec prints and the runner is quiet. The worst values are in M3-notes and in the failure messages.
§4.6's chain order gains the emission index as a last key, so the order is total.

Edge requires Definitions/Limits for CONTACT_TOL, beyond the plan's list of its requires. Edge.simplify takes an optional spend. Edge.profile returns RasterStats as a second value, as the plan's [3.2] has it.
The plan's per-traced-edge charge is 1 per crack edge visited, as the prototype does. Douglas–Peucker charges b − a per span looked at.
The fixture cores' names are valid blueprint names (≤ 32 code points, no '=', '°' or '×'), so they differ from the prototype's names; labels keep the prototype's names.
The shared record type is Build.Measured / Build.Expected in tests/fixtures/Build.luau. Regression and Cost tiers come from the plan's [7.2] (emulator, rank order).
A26's base is the variant 'A26base' of case A26, and A26's relation names a variant key. A25 and A27 are built from F1's parts; A26 is written from the prototype's rows.
Cost.TPERF holds {name, core, measureInvalid} entries, worst designs wrapped as cores, and P1 once as 'P1 (X08b)'.
The plan's 40-design fast Gen corpus is 20 (L12).
openIssues: For the lead (L3): with (b), Y translation can move EdgeLength on general designs (Gen #131 |ΔG| 0.0037), so O11 [Decision to confirm] carries it. The lattice rule (a) makes Y shifts exact on 898 copies but moves C15's Sharpening 0.4291 -> 0.4299. Its last-maximum variant passes the criterion; I did not adopt it because it is fitted to the fixtures. The lattice file is at m3-b1\work\out\Edge_lattice_a.luau in the scratchpad.

For the lead (new): exact-tie raster decisions are not translation-invariant, in the prototype too. These are cell centres on a face plane holding Z, exactly RASTER_TOL from one, or on a thin Wedge's sharp edge. C10 and C11 at +0.3317 move Sharpening G by 0.0063 and 0.0031, past TOL_G_INVARIANT 0.002 (a §5 promise on a calibration fixture). C09 under Z −0.037 changes cutIndex from 1 to 0.8842.

Tie fix options: tie-proof predicates in Physics/Shapes.chord (M2's) or keeping cell centres off part faces. Either moves fixture values. Reproductions: work\proto\yfix.luau, rasterdiff.luau and moves.luau in m3-b1.

Builder 3: add rungFits, raster, crackEdges, traceLoops, emitRun and simplify to Analyze.spec's long-loop names. Re-export Vec2, EdgeChain and EdgeProfile from Edge in Analyze. In phase 6, use Edge.profile(byRank, keptByRank, geometry, point, axis, spend) and Edge.cutIndex(physics.bladeLength, edge.bladeMeanThickness).
Builder 3: the plan's T-DIF-07(a) fixture list (F1, F3, F5, C02, C06) passes. Adding C10 or C11 at +0.3317 would fail TOL_G_INVARIANT (see above).
Builder 3: tiers in Regression and Cost records come from [7.2] (emulator). The goldens come from Analyze.run; trace any difference. A floating speck's tiers are those of its measureInvalid run.
Builder 4: O11 text with Gen #131's 0.0037; §4.6 and §17.2 wording for the raster ties; §16.32 TOL_EDGE_REL row; §16.18 guards (bladeLength floor 1e-6, Douglas–Peucker 1e-24 degenerate span).
